trendsArticle.topic: Can You Tell If Something Was Made by AI? The New Labeling Rules, Explained
trendsArticle.notes: Angle: a plain-language guide to how (and how reliably) people can now tell whether text, images, audio, or video was AI-made, pegged to the EU AI Act transparency rules that took effect Aug 2, 2026 requiring chatbots to disclose they're AI and deepfakes to be labeled. Ground via live search: the specifics of the EU rules, plus the watermarking/provenance moves from Anthropic (Claude), Google (SynthID), and OpenAI (C2PA), and consumer-facing signals like TikTok/LinkedIn labels. Be honest about limits — watermarks get stripped when content is edited or re-shared, and labels don't tell the full story. Avoid deep technical detail on cryptographic metadata; keep it about what a normal reader sees and should trust.

completed.rationale: The EU's AI transparency rules just came into force (Aug 2, 2026) and major labs simultaneously rolled out content watermarking, making 'is this real or AI?' an immediate, everyday concern for non-technical readers navigating deepfakes and synthetic media. The site covers agents, models, and safety but has no node on content provenance/labeling, so it fills a genuine gap. The topic is durable: the rules and labeling infrastructure are here to stay and will only grow more relevant over the coming month and beyond.

trendsArticle.topic: The AI Rules Taking Effect in 2026: What You Actually Need to Know
trendsArticle.notes: Plain-English guide to the regulations that are live or coming into force this year — EU AI Act obligations (GPAI transparency rules Aug 2026, high-risk system requirements), UK approach, US executive orders. Focus on what changes for everyday users and products, not legal detail. Ground via live search: which rules are in force now vs. coming soon, real examples of products affected. Avoid treating it as a law-school explainer — the angle is 'here is what is actually changing and why it matters to you'.
